biography.plain_text: William E. Boeing Jr. was an American businessman from Seattle and the son of the Boeing aircraft company’s founder. He developed industrial buildings and commercial warehouses, established the helicopter business AeroCopters and imported Volkswagen cars before dealerships became established. He also bought radio stations as part of his varied commercial interests.

long_biography.plain_text:
William E. Boeing Jr. helped preserve the Red Barn, the original Boeing aircraft factory, as a centrepiece of Seattle’s Museum of Flight. When port redevelopment threatened the building, he helped move it to the museum site in 1975. As a longstanding trustee, he supported the museum’s growth into an internationally recognised institution for aviation history and education.

Boeing and his wife June established the Aldarra Foundation in 2003. He stipulated that its assets should be spent within ten years of their deaths, directing substantial support towards organisations serving the Puget Sound region. Their interests included gardens for families facing cancer and research intended to improve patient care. The foundation subsequently funded patient navigation and cancer research at Fred Hutch.
long_biography.html:
William E. Boeing Jr. helped preserve the Red Barn, the original Boeing aircraft factory, as a centrepiece of Seattle’s Museum of Flight. When port redevelopment threatened the building, he helped move it to the museum site in 1975. As a longstanding trustee, he supported the museum’s growth into an internationally recognised institution for aviation history and education.

Boeing and his wife June established the Aldarra Foundation in 2003. He stipulated that its assets should be spent within ten years of their deaths, directing substantial support towards organisations serving the Puget Sound region. Their interests included gardens for families facing cancer and research intended to improve patient care. The foundation subsequently funded patient navigation and cancer research at Fred Hutch.
